method: Independent multi-agent adversarial re-derivation (3 agents, standalone /tmp python, no action_latent import, same fixed split).

key_checks: row-index / episode_uid / clip_idx sets pairwise DISJOINT across train(112)/val(24)/test(24); all 160 globally unique
suite stratification exact: 28/28/28/28 train, 6/6/6/6 val and test
cached e reconstructs in [train;val] order (err 2.4e-6); reversed order errs 12.4 -> pins ordering
train-only standardization stats differ materially from full-set (max mean diff 0.365) -> no full-set leakage
clip-level bootstrap CI width ~0.31 is ~5x the naive frame-level width ~0.06 -> clip-grouping correctly applied and material
split_and_methodology_audit.verdict: PASS — no cross-split contamination; e_to_a R2=0.5063 reproduced exactly.

env_shortcut_stress_test.verdict: Headroom is ROBUST. A nonlinear MLP on e gains only +0.05 (0.506->0.556) and plateaus far below the 0.935 ceiling; scene one-hots are negative. ~40% of the action-predictive ceiling lives outside W_env and cannot be recovered from e or scene labels.

ceiling_and_gain_rederivation.verdict: CONFIRMED — gain ~0.43 with CI cleanly excluding 0; test set is 24 clips (the '6/suite' is only the object-subset control).

important_caveat_pooling_convention.issue: Headline aggregate R2 pools the 7 action dims on RAW (unstandardized) actions, i.e. variance-weighted. High-variance dims (x,y,z,gripper) dominate; low-variance rotation dims (roll/pitch, std ~0.04-0.06) contribute little.
important_caveat_pooling_convention.impact: Both conventions defensible; per-dim R2 is identical (scale-invariant). The qualitative conclusion (large headroom, gain CI excludes 0, gate stays not-C/D) is unchanged. Most non-env headroom sits in the weak rotation dims — to watch in later phases.
important_caveat_pooling_convention.action_item: Phase 2+ should ALSO report equal-weight (per-dim-standardized) aggregate R2 alongside the variance-weighted one.

overall: All three independent re-derivations reproduce the M1 headline and find NO leakage. GATE-1 decisions (not-C/D; primary feature h_res) survive a stronger nonlinear env baseline. One transparency caveat: variance-weighted pooling inflates absolute magnitudes; report both conventions going forward.
